side_a: CC 2.6.1.1.1 "A field's definition MUST declare which kind it is; absent a declaration, set-semantics (sorted) is the default."
side_b: manifests/signed_object.cddl (CC 2.6.1.7) "? consent_basis: [* consent-basis],  ; OPTIONAL (capacity:*, observation:access_assumption:v1); default absent; array kind: sequence"
note: CC 2.1 defines consent_basis with no array kind, so the 2.6.1.1.1 default makes it a set (an unsorted or duplicated array is refused federation_set_semantics_unsorted); the 2.6.1.7 table and the CDDL make it a sequence kept as authored. The table applies the same default to differs_in in so many words, so one of the two is unstated: either CC 2.1 declares the sequence or the table reads set. The `paths` array inside each entry has no kind either.

side_a: CC 2.1 "`membership:proposal`, REQUIRED"
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 "REQUIRED on census:share:{class}:v1 and census:member:share:v1, where it is the period's end (census_return_expired after it)."
note: expires_at: CC 2.1 and CC 2.6.1.2 require it on a membership proposal; the 2.6.1.7 row (and the CDDL) gives presence OPTIONAL and names only the census shares as REQUIRED. CC 3.1.3.2 supports CC 2.1.

side_a: CC 2.1 "`membership:proposal`, nullable; restated on `membership:acceptance`"
side_b: CC 2.6.1.1.1 "an explicit JSON `null` on any optional envelope member is refused as malformed"
note: `role` is called nullable in CC 2.1 and its default is written `null` in CC 2.6.1.2; a null on the wire is refused envelope_member_null. 2.6.1.1.1 says a default written null means absent, and the 2.6.1.7 row says OPTIONAL, absent; 'nullable' is the stale word.

side_a: CC 2.6.2 "Every ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 datetime in this specification MUST be:"
side_b: manifests/signed_object.cddl (CC 2.6.1.7) "rfc3339 = tstr  ; a column rendered by the store; the signed twin inside the envelope is rfc3339-ms"
note: The columns beside the row (asserted_at, expires_at, scrub_timestamp, pqc_completed_at; valid_from and valid_until on a key record) are typed as an unconstrained string, while CC 2.6.2 binds every datetime to the millisecond Z form and cosigned_at beside the row is typed rfc3339-ms. Whether typed_diverges_from_envelope compares strings or instants is unstated. The vectors render every column in the millisecond form.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.1.1 "(no `0x`, no separators, byte-length-exact; never base64 in canonical bytes)"
side_b: CC 3.3.6.2 "The member carries both halves raw, in the standard base64 of [CC 2.6.1.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.1.1.1), and JCS sorts its keys:"
note: Rule 2 says public keys are lowercase hex and never base64 in canonical bytes; onion_hop_pubkeys, encryption_pubkeys and pubkey_ed25519_base64 / pubkey_ml_dsa_65_base64 (hashed into every recovery commitment, CC 3.2) are public keys in base64 inside signed bytes. The next sentence of rule 2 admits 'fields explicitly documented as base64', which is how a careful reader resolves it; CC 4.4.3.4.3.1 repeats 'pubkey byte fields are lowercase-hex' two paragraphs from a base64 public key.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.1.1 "elements MUST be **lexicographically sorted by their JCS string form (UTF-16 code-unit order, ascending)** before signing"
side_b: CC 3.4.7.1 "the set MUST be encoded as its members sorted ascending by Unicode code point, deduplicated, comma-joined with no whitespace"
note: Three orders are named for one rule: UTF-16 code units (2.6.1.1.1), Unicode code points (3.4.7.1) and UTF-8 bytes (CC 3.2 recovery commitments, CC 3.3.7 consent targets, CC 3.1.2.1 capability_declaration). Code-point and UTF-8 order agree with each other and differ from UTF-16 order above U+FFFF. Every set named today holds ASCII tokens, so no byte moves; an open-vocabulary set would fork.

side_a: CC 6.1.1 "**Leaf order MUST be lexicographic** over leaf bytes (the [CC 2.6.1.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md) set-semantics rule)."
side_b: CC 2.6.1.1.1 "elements MUST be **lexicographically sorted by their JCS string form (UTF-16 code-unit order, ascending)** before signing"
note: CC 6.1.1 sorts raw leaf bytes and names the 2.6.1.1.1 rule as its source, which sorts JCS strings by UTF-16 code unit. For a member id outside the BMP the two orders differ. CC 6.1.2.1.2 ('raw leaf bytes') and CC 6.1.5.2 ('sorted over UTF-8 bytes') support the byte reading; the citation is the loose part.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.3 "A CEG-Conforming Substrate (CCS) MUST preserve the as-received envelope object bytes for relay"
side_b: CC 2.6.1.1 "A relay that re-serializes from a parsed object at all MUST emit JCS"
note: Known, read as no conflict: 2.6.1.3 defines the contract as the as-received object (member set and values), and whitespace and member order are outside it. The word 'bytes' in the first sentence is still there.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.5 "`link_seq` is `u64` **big-endian** and monotonic per RNS Link (transit replay guard)."
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.5 "`link_seq` is a per-`(link, stream)` counter both ends keep and is never carried in the frame"
note: Known, resolution 'to fix from the text': NOT yet fixed, both sentences stand at head 87c1730. A per-link counter and a per-(link, stream) counter give different outer nonces on a link that carries two streams, so frames fail to open.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.3 "is a 64-byte Ed25519 signature by the bound chunk key, appended to the inner unit after the inner ciphertext and inside the outer seal"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.3 "the shipping form, which precedes the signature with an 8-byte publisher timestamp `source_ms` under the domain `ciris-edge:av-chunk-sig:v2`"
note: Known, resolution 'to fix from the text': NOT yet fixed. The section still lays out the v1 trailer in full and names the v2 form (with source_ms) as the shipping one without its layout; a relay built to either refuses the other's chunks as av_chunk_trailer_invalid.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.3 "32 bytes (caller-derived: sha256(stream_meta))"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.3 "`stream_id` (32 bytes, which MUST equal `SHA-256("ciris-edge:call-stream:v2" ‖ room ‖ publisher ‖ join_nonce)` with no length prefixes)"
note: The byte layout's comment derives stream_id from an undefined stream_meta; the binding rule in the same section fixes the derivation for a call stream and a receiver re-derives it. The MUST governs; the comment is loose, and no derivation is given for a stream that is not a call.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.5 "the **outer** seal is the per-RNS-Link transit wrap (a relay sees the outer layer only, never plaintext"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.3 "under the [CC 5.3.3.2.5](#5.3.3.2.5) outer seal (AES-256-GCM), itself inside the link's [CC 5.3.3.5](#5.3.3.5) E1 transit seal"
note: One sentence makes the outer seal the transit wrap itself (two layers, 'the E1 two-layer posture'); the other puts the outer seal inside a separate E1 transit seal (three layers); CC 5.4.2 says the chunk rides 'under the E1 seal'. The outer-nonce vectors pin the bytes, so a reader resolves it there, but the text names the layers two ways.

side_a: CC 5.3.2.5 "A blob cited only by a bare `evidence_refs[]` string has no declared size, and a consumer fetching it enforces the [CC 2.6.1.3](part_2_the_grammar.md) cap instead."
side_b: CC 2.6.1.3 "the heavy payload moves to the blob plane as encrypted chunks, replicated per item to the holder count its owner chose"
note: The 2.6.1.3 cap is 1 MiB on an envelope's JCS bytes. Read onto a blob it refuses any bare-cited blob above 1 MiB, which is the very payload 2.6.1.3 sends to the blob plane and names 'by content hash in evidence_refs'. The two agree only if every above-cap payload is cited through a descriptor that carries its size (trace_manifest:v1 does); neither sentence says so.

side_a: CC 6.1.3 "the holding claim, the compress request and the capacity preimage — are **transport/substrate framing**: binary, never a CC 2.1 Contribution"
side_b: CC 2.1 "subscribers discover holders through the holding claims at the content's scope (`custody:ack:v1` `here` rows"
note: 'Holding claim' names two objects with two wire forms: the custody:ack:v1 row, a CC 2.1 row under JCS (Parts 2, 3, 5), and the chunk-level binary claim of CC 6.1.5 (Part 6). CC 6.1.5 calls the second 'the chunk-level companion of the whole-blob custody:ack:v1 report', which resolves it; CC 6.1.3's flat 'never a CC 2.1 Contribution' does not say which it means.

side_a: CC 3.4.11 "Parsers MUST tolerate the trailing `:vN` version segment."
side_b: CC 3.1.7 "A dimension without it is refused with **`missing_version_segment`**, never admitted as a second leaf beside its versioned sibling."
note: 'Tolerate' reads as optional; CC 3.1.7 requires the segment on every dimension but the two exempt families, and the next sentence of CC 3.4.11 gives both arities with {version}. The 3.1.7 rule governs; the 'tolerate' sentence is older wording.

side_a: CC 3.1.2 "Carries no version segment (`_meta.case_rule.version_segment.exempt`): the suffix is the hash."
side_b: CC 3.1.7 "Two families need none, and a tail on one is tolerated, never required"
note: Known and settled from the text: the matcher and the manifest admit an exempt family with or without a tail. The CC 3.1.2 row still reads as 'has none'.

side_a: CC 3.3.2 "The wrap is `wrap_algorithm` (v2 only) and `wrapped_dek`."
side_b: CC 3.3.2 "HPKE RFC 9180 base-mode shape; X25519 KEM + HKDF-SHA-256 KDF + AES-256-GCM AEAD. **v1**."
note: Known, held. 'v2 only' and CC 5.1 ('A DEK that is wrapped MUST be wrapped with wrap_algorithm: v2 ... never v1') against a closed-set table that still registers the v1 string and makes v2 mandatory 'for streaming epoch-DEK grants' only. A consumer MUST reject v1 only on a streaming epoch grant (CC 5.1), so a v1 wrap on a content grant is admitted by one reading and refused by the other.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 "REQUIRED on supersedes, withdraws, recants"
side_b: CC 2.1 "With `references_attestation_id` it binds an answer to exactly one proposal"
note: Known, held: the table types references_attestation_id as the composer target on the three composers, and CC 2.1 and Part 3 use it on scores rows (membership answers). Still as it was.

side_a: CC 5.3.2.4.2 "Registry owns the exact envelope member set ([CC 2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md) + the [CC 2.6.1.2](part_2_the_grammar.md) catalog)"
side_b: CC 2.6.1.3 "`attestation_envelope`, whose member set and placement are pinned at [CC 2.6.1.7](#2.6.1.7)"
note: Two homes are named for the member set: CC 2.1 plus the 2.6.1.2 catalogue (which is marked informational) and the 2.6.1.7 table. The same paragraph of 5.3.2.4.2 calls the object contribution_envelope where 2.6.1.7 calls it attestation_envelope. 2.6.1.7 is the home.

side_a: CC 2.3.2.1 "Registry key_ids are themselves hex fingerprints, not base64 pubkeys"
side_b: CC 2.6.8 "`key_id = "<label>-<fingerprint>"`, `fingerprint` = the first **10 base32 characters** (50 bits) of `sha256(ed25519_pubkey)`, lowercased"
note: The reason given for the mandatory tag describes key ids as hex fingerprints; the same paragraph and CC 2.6.8 make the current form label plus a base32 fingerprint, hex being the older form a directory may still hold. Both readers keep the tag; the sentence is stale.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 "`subject_key_id_malformed` (an element of `subject_key_ids` is neither a `key_id` nor the tagged canonical form of [CC 2.3.2.1](#2.3.2.1))"
side_b: manifests/signed_object_vectors.json "subject_key_ids element malformed (canonical prefix is not lowercase)"
note: Two refusal vectors carry a description where the text gives a token from a closed set: refuse_subject_uppercase_tag (above) and refuse_cohort_scope_unknown ('cohort_scope not in the closed set', where the text gives federation_malformed_row with a reason). A second implementation cannot match its token against either.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.3 "The cross-impl JCS vector set MUST include a non-representable-number case (a value with no finite double, asserted to reject)"
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 "a cosigned variant; a `withdraws`; the at-cap and cap-plus-one envelopes as a recipe with their hashes; and refusal cases with their tokens"
note: manifests/signed_object_vectors.json holds 14 vectors. None is the non-representable number (2.6.1.3 MUST), the base64-variant round trip (2.6.1.1.1 MUST), an explicit null (envelope_member_null) or an unsorted or duplicated set (federation_set_semantics_unsorted). The set-against-sequence, hex and timestamp cases are present.

side_a: CC 2.3.2.1 "`{hashalg}` is exactly `sha256` for v1; an exact tag admits neither case variance nor whitespace."
side_b: manifests/signed_object.cddl "canonical-id = tstr .regexp "canonical:[a-z0-9-]+:[0-9a-f]+"  ; CC 2.3.2.1, tag required"
note: The schema admits canonical:md5:… and a digest of any length, both reject vectors of CC 2.3.2.1 (which wants sha256 and exactly 64 hex). The comment points at the section, so a reader who follows it refuses them; one who validates by the schema alone admits them.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 "`envelope_member_invalid` (a member is ill-typed or an instant is not in the [CC 2.6.2](#2.6.2) form)"
side_b: manifests/family_model.json "signed instants .sssZ only (signed_instant_form_violation)"
note: The freshness cell of every family names a refusal token, signed_instant_form_violation, that appears nowhere in Parts 1 to 8; the text and the refuse_timestamp_form vector give federation_malformed_row with reason envelope_member_invalid for the same refusal.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.6 "For accountable streams, "published" means **witness-cosigned** (the CC 5.3.1 path), so the subscriber cannot collude with the producer on a private root."
side_b: CC 8.10 "attest: `one transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size}@admitted[val:log_id=leaf:stream_id,val:root_hash=val:chunk_root,leaf:tree_size>=val:K] else refuse` (CC 5.3.3.6)"
note: The card of delivery_receipt:{stream_id} refuses every receipt that has no cosigned head. The text asks for a published head, and makes 'published' mean witness-cosigned for accountable streams only; a best-effort stream publishes producer-signed roots alone (CC 5.3.3.3, witness cosign OPTIONAL). A receipt on a best-effort stream is admitted by the text and refused by the card, if transparency_log:cosigned is the witness-cosigned head as its name says.

side_a: CC 3.1.3 "**Yes — self only, by possession**; every other row is admitted only once its signer's `key:record` is held (retryable otherwise)"
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 "Self-scrub when equal to key_id; an anchor scrub when it names a pinned anchor (the one record kind where the scrubber may differ from the subject)."
note: CC 2.4 and CC 3.1.3 admit a key record signed by the key itself, by proof of possession, and make an anchor scrub 'a cosignature' beside it. The 2.6.1.7 table lets the record's own scrub_key_id name an anchor, so the base signature is not the key's. A new record whose base scrub is an anchor's is admitted by the table's reader and refused by the other. The family model's note ('pre-rc8 anchor-scrubbed base admitted') suggests the table describes records already held; the CC 8.10 card says attest: self.

side_a: CC 3.4.7 "Every admission decision above MUST be made against the `federation_keys` row's `identity_type` set"
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 "Serialised as roles; the record also carries roles inside the signed registration_envelope."
note: A key record carries its role set three ways: identity_type ('a set rendered as one string'), a roles array beside the record and roles inside the signed envelope. CC 3.4.7 says the gate reads identity_type and never a role inside the envelope; nothing says whether the roles array beside the record is the same set, or what holds when the two differ. CC 3.4.7.1 leaves the storage form to the implementer.

side_a: CC 2.6.8 "a consumer resolving a `key_id` MUST verify the fingerprint against the pubkey it obtains"
side_b: CC 2.3.2.1 "A consumer verifies a `key_id`'s fingerprint suffix against the public key it obtains **at registration and at pairing**"
note: Known and settled from the text as one act with its scope stated in CC 2.3.2.1. CC 2.6.8 still says 'resolving' and, in the next sentence, 'detected at registration and never at resolution'.

side_a: CC 2.3.2.2 "the binding is itself a `delegates_to`-shaped attestation"
side_b: CC 3.3.14 "A bare `scores` Contribution on the registered dimension **`identity:canonical_binding:{canonical_hash}`**"
note: Known (proposed, not applied; for Eric). The row type of a canonical binding is delegates_to in CC 2.3.2.2 and scores in CC 3.3.14, and the two sections also differ on whether the binding opens rule 2. Still as it was.

side_a: CC 3.3.13 "`evidence_refs[]` stays bare sha256."
side_b: CC 3.3.13 "digest          sha256:<hex>   over the bytes as stored and forwarded; == evidence_refs[]"
note: Whether the string in evidence_refs[] is 64 hex characters or `sha256:` followed by them. 'Bare' is said against a CID or multihash wrapper, and the field set and the signed-object vector (`sha256:9f86…`) carry the prefixed form; CC 5.3.2.5 says 'a bare URI or content-hash string'. A producer writing the unprefixed digest would fail the digest == evidence_refs[] comparison at a reader of the field set.

side_a: CC 3.3.13 "codec           string         RFC 6381 family; REQUIRED for video/mp4, audio/mp4"
side_b: CC 3.3.13 "**`format` and `codec` are required in clear iff `sealed_descriptor` is ABSENT.**"
note: The rule reads as requiring codec in clear on every unsealed struct, an image included; the field set and the codec bullet require it for video/mp4 and audio/mp4 only, and the seal carries it 'where applicable'. The field set is the narrower and the consistent one.

side_a: CC 3.3.13 "over the descriptor members `name`, `format` and, where applicable, `codec` (a JCS object)"
side_b: CC 3.3.13 "AEAD seal under the room DEK over {name, format, codec?, parent?} as a JCS object,"
note: The prose lists three sealed members; the field set lists four and says `parent` exists ONLY inside the seal. CC 3.1.3.4 depends on the sealed parent, so the field set is right and the prose list is short by one.

side_a: CC 3.3.13 "the address `digest`, the room target, `content_digest` in the encrypted two-hash case, and `placeholder`"
side_b: CC 3.3.13 "placeholder     {thumbhash}    ~25 bytes, decoded by arithmetic — the only element a UI may show before CC 5.3.2.5 has passed"
note: 'In clear, always required' names placeholder and a room target. The field set marks only size REQUIRED, gives placeholder no force (and it has no meaning for audio), and has no member for the room target.

side_a: CC 3.3.13 "**Shape: HLS / CMAF over fragmented MP4 (RFC 8216)**, so chunks and files share one schema."
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.2 "with an application-defined payload codec in place of an A/V codec"
note: CC 3.3.13 fixes a live_stream chunk as one fMP4 segment whose concatenation is a valid video/mp4. CC 5.3.3.2.1 and 5.3.3.2.2 make the realtime chunk payload opaque and application-defined (game ticks, CRDT operations, one chunk per ChunkLayer cell) on the same live_stream wire. A substrate cannot see inside a sealed chunk, so admission does not differ; what a recording of such a stream is, and whether it is attested as video, does.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.1 "the codec itself is named by the stream's binding, never by this id, which carries layer semantics only"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.3 "`epoch` (u64, the room's MLS epoch); `chunk_key` (32 bytes, the Ed25519 public key)"
note: The StreamKeyBinding of 5.3.3.2.3 is a closed fixed encoding (version, room, publisher, join_nonce, stream_id, epoch, chunk_key, two signatures) with no codec member and trailing bytes refused. The codec is a stream field of the CC 3.3.13 descriptor. 'The stream's binding' in 5.3.3.2.1 names something other than the binding the next section defines.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.4 "Every `codec_id` class defines a floor layer, a presence tile of colour and a blink at one frame a second"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.1 "No scalable-coding semantics. `ChunkLayer` MUST be `{ 0, 0, 0 }`. Default for non-layered streams and for audio."
note: The opaque class 0xFF has one layer and carries audio; it has no floor tile to define, and 5.3.3.2.1 says 'an opaque stream is base'. 'Every codec_id class' should read every layered class.

side_a: CC 3.3.13 "the substrate never holds a room DEK on the row plane and never renders"
side_b: CC 5.3.2.6 "The ingest pipeline that makes Tier A enforceable belongs on the **node**, so every client renders only bytes the node's safe encoder produced."
note: For sealed content the node that stores and forwards cannot decode, so it cannot run demux, re-encode or strip; CC 3.3.13 also says the node 'stores and forwards verbatim' and that the hash authority MUST NOT re-encode, while the tier table has WebP 're-encoded on ingest'. They agree if 'node' in 5.3.2.6 is the opener's own node and its output is a rendition with derived_from; 5.3.2.6 says neither, and its table is marked recommended, not normative.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2 "pull-only `ContentFetch` (CC 5.3.3.5 E2), as for broadcast; no selective-forwarding relay role"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.4 "a relay forwards only the layers downstream asked for"
note: Known, for Eric, nothing in the text decides: whether a call's chunks pass through member relays (5.3.3.4 layered multipath, 5.3.3.2.3 'a member relay verifies', 5.4.6 'the tree's relays') or only over direct links and pull (5.3.3.2 profiles, CC 2.1 'never through a relay tree'). Still as it was.
